html:
The Gudanji, also known as the Kotandji or Ngandji, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory, in the country inland from the Gulf of Carpentaria on the northern edge of the Barkly Tableland.

Their language belongs to the West Barkly group, with those of the Wambaya and Binbinga. Other neighbours were the Gunindiri, Jingili and Alawa. Cattle stations reached this grassland in the 1880s, and the language is now endangered.
